otherConditions: Legislated window: 'within twelve months from the date of shipment' (was nine months until 28.02.2018; 14/2018-Cus(NT)). windowDays=365 approximates calendar months.

Only 'in exceptional cases where the certificate of origin has not been issued before the time limit' (normal issuance: not later than three days from date of shipment), at the request of the exporter or its authorised agent, per exporting Party's laws.
'ISSUED RETROACTIVELY' box ticked in Box/Field 8 (Remarks) and the date of shipment (B/L or AWB date) indicated in Box 3.
Para 3(c): an importer without a COO at importation may apply for refund of excess duty on later presentation of the COO.

transitConditions: Transported directly from the other Party; or

transported through one or more non-Parties for transit or temporary storage in warehouses, provided it does not undergo operations other than unloading, reloading and any other operation to preserve it in good condition.
No 'control of customs authority' or 'geographical reason' condition in this agreement.
documentsRequired: Customs may require: (a) copy of through bill of lading indicating port of exportation and importation; or (b) certificate/other information from customs of the non-Party or other relevant entities evidencing no operations beyond unloading/reloading/preservation (Annexure-2 para 2(3), p28).
Both (a) and (b) may be required where the container was opened, seal number changed, container number changed, or package opened (Appendix-A para 13, p35).

source.quote: (b) transported through one or more non-Parties for the purpose of transit or temporary storage in warehouses in such non-Parties, subject to the condition that it does not undergo operations other than unloading, reloading and any other operation to preserve it in good condition.

conditions: COO not refused only because the invoice is issued by a person located in a non-Party (Appendix-A para 7, p34).
Where invoice issuer differs from the exporter and is in a non-Party: tick 'Third Country Invoicing' and give full legal name and address of the invoicing person in Field 8 (p38).

If the non-Party invoice number is not known at COO issuance, Field 7 shows the exporter's invoice no./date, box ticked, invoicer named in Field 8; customs may require invoices and documents confirming the transaction (p38).

source.quote: The customs authority of the importing Party shall not refuse to accept a certificate of origin only for the reason that the invoice is issued by either a natural person or a juridical person located in a non-Party.

cumulation: bilateral (India-Japan) accumulation, rule 7 - originating good of the other Party used as material counts as originating if last production process goes beyond rule 9 operations; marked 'ACU' in Field 5
notes: Certificate title observed on ex_job6: "COMPREHENSIVE ECONOMIC PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT BETWEEN JAPAN AND THE REPUBLIC OF INDIA" (Japan-issued certificates put Japan first). Validity: single importation, 12 months from issuance; COO submitted after expiry due to force majeure 'shall be accepted' (p29). Lost COO: new COO marked 'CERTIFIED TRUE COPY' in Box 8, valid for original term (p33). Two or more invoices for a single shipment may be shown on one COO (para 6, p33). Goods not eligible for preference may appear on the COO; COO valid only for the eligible goods (para 8, p34). Paragraph 9 of Annexure-2 is missing in the gazette text (numbering jumps 8->10, p31). S.No.3 quota goods (vanaspati 100,000 MT, acrylic yarn 10,000 MT, copper 10,000 MT, zinc oxide 2,500 MT per 6 March-5 March year) need both conditions 2 and 3.
